page: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with 16 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Storage is provided via a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance runs on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also strong for large-block read-only operations, reaching 184.1 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory score is highly rated. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. The server demonstrates strong bzip3 decompression speeds for both single-threaded and multi-threaded tasks, while other operations like gzip compression, software compilation, and ray tracing perform at average levels.

Given its dedicated compute cores and 2.0 GB of RAM per core, the c3-32 offers a balanced profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as text processing, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference, where text generation for a 135M model achieves a strong rate of 283.36 tokens/sec. The inclusion of local NVMe storage supports database operations and web serving, which perform at average baseline levels. This hardware profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency by providing dedicated physical cores and fast local storage without the overhead of high-capacity memory allocations.
description: The OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized server instance utilizing the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It delivers 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 2.0 GB per core. The instance features 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps on a KVM hypervisor. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance and large-block read memory bandwidth, alongside average multi-core and database execution speeds. Lacking a GPU, this server is designed for non-accelerated, compute-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for software compilation, text processing, bzip3 decompression, and small-scale language model inference.
